name: StillPoint

temporal_authority.governing_rule: A successful description must not acquire permanent jurisdiction over the thing it describes.
enforced: claims and predictions do not self-authorize actions
warrants are domain, action, scope, and time bounded
expired, revoked, completed, superseded, released, or review-required warrants cannot authorize execution
material later evidence can force supporting authority into review
cross-domain claim use requires an explicit bridge
historical claims and evidence survive supersession and release
terminal runtime warrants are not silently reissued under the same authority revision
approval cannot revive a non-current temporal warrant
warrant changes during adapter execution prevent false completion
re-entry creates a new auditable evaluation rather than rewriting prior state
founder, administrator, and provider identity do not bypass warrant state

known_limitations: The temporal ledger is currently a Python runtime API; dedicated CLI inspection and operator commands are not yet exposed.

Runtime-generated external-action warrants are bound to the current CEO request and policy authority revision; domain applications that rely on substantive factual claims must explicitly attach those claims through the temporal ledger.
A warrant invalidated during a real adapter call cannot undo an external side effect already emitted; StillPoint preserves the external result, blocks false completion, and requires review/re-entry.
